gaps.sentence: He ___ me of leaking the story to the press.
gaps.explanation: Accuse somebody of + -ing. Blame uses 'for', thank and congratulate use different prepositions.

gaps.sentence: 'I'm sorry I forgot the meeting,' she said. She ___ forgetting the meeting.
gaps.explanation: An apology is reported with 'apologised for + gerund'.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll have finished by noon,' she promised. She promised she ___ finished by noon.
gaps.explanation: will have + past participle becomes would have + past participle.

gaps.sentence: 'I was living in Berlin at the time,' she recalled. She recalled that she ___ living in Berlin at the time.
gaps.explanation: Past continuous backshifts to past perfect continuous: was living → had been living.

gaps.sentence: 'I'm sorry I shouted at you,' he said. He ___ shouting at me.
gaps.explanation: Apologies take apologise for + -ing: apologised for shouting.

gaps.sentence: 'Do you know the way?' she asked me. She asked me ___ the way.
gaps.explanation: Do you know → if I knew: no do-support in the reported clause.

gaps.sentence: 'We'll be arriving on the red-eye,' they said. They said they ___ on the red-eye.
gaps.explanation: 'Will be arriving' backshifts to 'would be arriving'.

gaps.sentence: 'You broke my phone!' she said to her brother. She ___ her brother of breaking her phone.
